newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL blue-chips end weaker on foreign fund sales.
newsitem.headline: KL blue-chips end weaker on foreign fund sales.

text.p: Selling by some foreign funds pulled Kuala Lumpur blue chips to a lower finish on Wednesday, while secondary counters continued to rebound.
"There was a sell program in the market today," said one dealer. Said an analyst with a local research house, "What I understand was there was a bit of selling by the foreign funds."

The benchmark Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange Composite Index finished down 2.16 points to 1,140.92. Buyers continued to pour into the Second Board, boosting the index up 14.97 points or 2.65 percent to 579.65.

Turnover was moderately heavy amid this week's elections of the dominant United Malays National Organisation (UMNO) party. At the close, over 245 million shares changed hands and losers outpaced gainers by 323 to 258.
Noting that volume has been subdued during previous UMNO election weeks, Audrey Ho, head of research at Mohaiyani Securities said, "This is expected."
Also to be expected is the resurgence of the Second Board following its recent correction, she said. "It will continue to hog the limelight. It will probably test 630 again."
